title: C06 — Project assessment and evidence verification

sections.title: 1. Purpose of C06 and scope of this page

blocks.content: C06 brings specification, architecture, quality, detailed design and tests into one assessment. We check whether claims about the reservation system match the code and observable behavior of the same version.

The source is SWI_C06_Assessment_Form_CZ_v4.md. The assessment produces a completed form with evidence, verified or rejected candidate findings, and the project owner’s response. This page explains what each part covers and why we have it.

This page is a guide and evidence map for assessing OP-05, not a completed assessment form. It distinguishes inspected code and test definitions, historically recorded results, and checks still to be performed. Final YES / PARTLY / NO / N/A ratings require evidence for the specific assessed version.

items: Identify a shared baseline for documentation, code and tests and verify that it runs.
Trace one concrete path from a requirement through design to a test.
Examine a measurable quality criterion and what its result means.
Verify candidate findings and record the owner’s decision.

sections.title: 2. The scenario we use in this project

blocks.content: Our selected path is OP-05 — reservation approval. It connects C02, C03 and C05 and has a concrete implementation and tests. Using one scenario lets us follow the same claim across all parts.

headers: Why we have it / where to look
rows: Operation: the slot owner approves a PENDING reservation.
The teacher decides on requests for their slot. C02, section 12, OP-05 / REQ-05.
Invariant BR-02: at most one active reservation per slot; both PENDING and CONFIRMED block it.
Approval must not release an occupied slot. C02 domain rules and state model.
Responsibility owner: ReservationService.approve.
Rules and transaction coordination belong in one place. C03B and docs/architecture-and-decisions.md.
ADR-01: actor identity comes from authenticated sign-in.
A client must not impersonate another teacher when approving. docs/architecture-and-decisions.md, ADR-01.
C05 unit: reservation approval, history and notification.
State, the audit record and the student’s notification must stay consistent. C05 design and verification evidence.

blocks.content: Scope: one approval through POST /api/reservations/{reservationId}/approve and the corresponding service method. A notification means an internal record in the notifications table; we do not demonstrate email delivery or that the student read it. BR-02 is a related invariant, not proof that concurrent approval of the same reservation cannot produce duplicate side effects.

The form header records the assessing team, assessed team, project, assessed commit/tag and date. Our project is Consultation Reservation. An exact commit/tag prevents comparing an old diagram with new code or test results from a different version.

rows: B1
One precisely identified version of documentation, code and tests.

Record the full commit hash. If local changes exist, preserve their exact contents, including new files, or first create an assessable commit. git status lists changes but does not preserve their contents.
B2
The relevant product or tests can be run.
README.md and DOCKER.md describe startup; record the command, environment and result of an actual run. Instructions alone do not prove a successful run.

blocks.content: Use git rev-parse HEAD and git status --short to identify the version. Start the app from the repository root with docker compose up --build. Tests require the environment described in C05, including Java 21 and PostgreSQL for integration cases.

A baseline is a fixed version of the assessed artifacts. This guide does not declare a final assessed commit/tag. A run record needs the date, Java/PostgreSQL versions, command, test/failure/error/skip counts and retained reports. A successful frontend build is not evidence of a successful backend test.

sections.title: 4. C02 — Specification: what the system should do

rows: R1

The service takes a reservation UUID, AuthenticatedUser and a non-null ReservationTransitionRequest; note may be null. Success requires an existing reservation, active TEACHER role, slot ownership and PENDING.

C02 OP-05 specifies CONFIRMED and history. The C05 contract elaborates this with confirmedAt and an internal notification. The HTTP endpoint accepts a JSON object, such as {}; identity comes from @AuthenticationPrincipal, not the request body.
R2
BR-02 permits at most one PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation for the same slot_id.

Concrete protection: backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_reservation_schema.sql, index one_active_reservation_per_slot. SQL inspection establishes the constraint definition; deployment and concurrent behavior require runtime evidence.
R3
Approval transitions PENDING → CONFIRMED; neither CANCELLED nor CONFIRMED may be approved again.
The operation must agree with the state model. C02 state diagram and C05 transitions.
R4
ReservationService.approve checks identity, role, input, ownership and state before changing the reservation.
Compare promised behavior with actual code, beyond the endpoint description. ReservationService.java and Reservation.confirm.
R5
The test sources include success and rejection of another teacher and invalid states.

ReservationAuthorizationTests: ownerApprovesWithoutClientActorId, otherTeacherCannotSpoofOwnerWhenApproving, ownerCannotApproveTwice, ownerCannotApproveCancelledReservation. Test existence is not a run result, and this suite does not test BR-02 database exclusivity.
Missing actor / active role is not TEACHER
ApiException 401 / 403 before reading the reservation, for a direct service call. An unauthenticated HTTP request may be rejected by the security filter; the existing HTTP test requires only 4xx.
Missing ID or request / reservation does not exist
After actor checks: 400 for null ID or request, then 404 for a missing reservation. A malformed UUID or missing JSON body at the HTTP layer is a different case.
Another teacher / owner with an invalid state
403 for another teacher takes precedence over the state check; the owner gets 409 for CONFIRMED or CANCELLED. No state, history or notification changes.
Owner + PENDING, without a technical failure
HTTP 200; CONFIRMED, confirmedAt, exactly one new history record and internal notification within one call. A separate integration suite verifies the database commit.

sections.title: 5. C03 — Architecture: who owns each responsibility

rows: A1
The reservation service owns approval rules and transaction coordination; the entity owns the state change.
Every responsibility needs an explicit owner. C03B and C05 responsibility allocation.
A2
The controller delegates, ReservationService decides and Reservation.confirm sets state and confirmedAt.

Reservation.confirm does not check previous state or authorization itself. The guarantee therefore belongs to the service path. JPA persists the managed entity at flush/commit; approve does not call reservations.save().
A3
Filter → controller → service: actor, role and null inputs → load reservation → load user → ownership → PENDING → confirm → history → notification.

ReservationService.approve performs initial checks before reading data. When called through the Spring proxy, the transaction commits before the result returns to the controller; a flush/commit failure can prevent a successful HTTP response.
A4
ADR-01: sign-in determines identity. The only declared ReservationTransitionRequest field is note; unknown fields, including actorUserId, are ignored.

api/ReservationController.java, api/ReservationTransitionRequest.java and otherTeacherCannotSpoofOwnerWhenApproving. The test uses the real filter/controller/service but replaces AuthService; it does not prove the full sign-in process or the security of every endpoint.

blocks.content: C03A describes the historical state before the identity fix. In docs/evidence-and-evolution.md, the original Evidence C03B is explicitly marked historical and updated with its resolution: the controller passes AuthenticatedUser and client-supplied actorUserId is ignored. This conclusion comes from code and test inspection; the assessed baseline still needs corresponding run evidence.

sections.title: 6. C04 — Quality and measurement: how we decide

blocks.content: For C06, we propose a single-approval integrity criterion: all three scenarios below must pass on the same baseline, with no failures, errors or skips. History and notification counts are scoped to the tested reservation. The criterion checks atomic persistence under specific controlled failures, not general system reliability.

There is currently no separate C04 tab in the documentation navigation. This is a proposed assessment criterion based on C05 design and tests, not a claim that a completed C04 deliverable already exists.

rows: successfulApprovalCommitsStateHistoryAndNotification

Before: PENDING, confirmedAt = null, history 1, notifications 1. After: CONFIRMED, non-null confirmedAt, history 2, notifications 2; the new history actor is the owner and the new notification recipient is the student.
historyFailureRollsBackApproval
After forcing reservation and history writes, an IllegalStateException is injected. A new SQL read returns the original PENDING, null, 1, 1; the notification service is not called.
notificationFailureRollsBackApprovalAndHistory
After actually creating the notification and flushing all writes, an IllegalStateException is injected. Following rollback, a new SQL read returns the original PENDING, null, 1, 1.
Q1
The criterion specifies expected state and record counts for both success and failure.
An assessor must be able to decide pass/fail. C05 atomic persistence and rollback.
Q2
Measurement uses an actual Spring transaction and PostgreSQL, with results read in a new transaction.
Mocks cannot prove database rollback. ReservationApprovalPersistenceTests covers one commit and two controlled failures after writes.
Q3
If 3/3 cases pass, retain the transaction design for the verified scope. On failure, investigate the cause; if skipped or unable to run, record missing evidence.
The result does not prove concurrency, resilience to a DB connection outage or delivery outside the database. The historical C05 run is not automatically a new C06 measurement.

blocks.content: C05 records a historical successful run on 2026-10-19: 26 backend tests, including three persistence tests. For C06, the assessor must establish how that run relates to the assessed baseline or rerun the tests. Source: docs/evidence-and-evolution.md, C05 DD Verification Evidence.

Measurement context: the test creates a c05_test_… schema using Flyway, commits initial data before calling the service and invokes it through the Spring transaction proxy. The test is not wrapped in an automatically rolled-back test transaction. Spies inject failure after actual SQL writes; verification then reads the database in a new transaction.

sections.title: 7. C05 — Detailed design and unit verification

rows: D1
Unit intent: only the owner approves a PENDING reservation, with accurate history and a student notification.
Design explains the purpose, beyond a list of methods. C05 goal and responsibilities.
D2
The design matches the checks, confirm call and subsequent writes in approve.
Design/code differences can change behavior. C05 algorithm and ReservationService.approve.
D3
Each test follows from a contract or design decision.
Tests should verify intended behavior. C05 D1–D6 decision mapping and ReservationApprovalDesignTests.
D4
Test cases cover the listed rejection branches, all three reservation states, success and two controlled failure types.

This is a mapping of tests to design, not a measured coverage percentage. It provides no evidence for concurrent approvals or all technical failures. Sequential 409 behavior does not prove safe concurrency.
D5
ownerApprovesWithCorrectAuditAndStudentNotification checks CONFIRMED, its timestamp, the history actor and notification recipient.
The oracle is a concrete expected outcome; merely not throwing an exception would miss incorrect history or recipients.

blocks.content: D1–D5 in this table identify C06 assessment questions. D1–D6 within C05 identify design decisions; these are separate sets of identifiers.

sections.title: 8. How to record a rating and evidence

blocks.content: The form specifies rating names and requires evidence but does not define detailed decision rules. The following is our working interpretation; actual use must follow the assessor’s rules. Missing evidence is distinct from demonstrated noncompliance.

rows: YES
The requirement is supported within the assessed scope. Cite concrete evidence.
PARTLY
Only part is supported. State what holds and what is missing.
NO
The requirement is not met or the necessary evidence is missing; specify which applies.
N/A
The question does not apply to the selected scope. Explain why.

blocks.content: Every form row needs Evidence / comment. Useful evidence includes the baseline, file and method or document section, verification procedure, and expected and observed results. A test name points to what to verify; a run report records what actually happened.

sections.title: 9. Candidate findings F1–F3 and owner disposition

blocks.content: The form provides three slots, F1–F3, for candidate findings. A suspicion becomes a verified finding only after comparing the claim with evidence and performing verification. A finding need not require a code change: it may concern inconsistent documentation or insufficient evidence.

rows: Source + Engineering claim
The exact source and claim being checked, so the intended behavior is clear.
Expected + Observed
Expected and observed behavior separately, making the difference explicit.
Evidence + Verification performed
Baseline, artifact references, procedure and result so the check can be repeated.
Result
VERIFIED FINDING or REJECTED CANDIDATE based on the verification performed.

blocks.content: Example candidate, not a newly confirmed finding: two concurrent approvals may create duplicate history or notifications. C05 records this as a risk. Verification needs a concurrent scenario on an identified baseline and inspection of stored records; a sequential repeat-approval test is insufficient.

rows: ACCEPTED
The owner accepts the finding and records a reason/evidence and a concrete action.
REJECTED
The owner rejects the finding with a reason/evidence and explains why no change is needed.
DEFERRED
The owner postpones resolution, recording a reason and a follow-up action.

blocks.content: For each finding, retain the Finding, owner decision, Reason/evidence and Action / no-change. Verification by the assessor and disposition by the owner are two separate steps.

sections.title: 10. Where the evidence lives and what we deliver

items: C02: frontend/src/features/docs/c02/en.json — OP-05, BR-02 and the state model.
C03 and C05: docs/architecture-and-decisions.md — responsibilities, ADR-01 and detailed design.
Historical run evidence and acknowledged limitations: docs/evidence-and-evolution.md.
Implementation: backend/src/main/java/consultation_reservation_backend/ — api/ReservationController.java, service/ReservationService.java and domain types.
Report location after execution: backend/target/surefire-reports/. Reports are generated and may be overwritten by the next run; retain a copy with the baseline identification.

blocks.content: The commands below reproduce verification from the repository root; they are not a log of a new successful run. Use Java 21. The first selection does not require PostgreSQL; the second requires it on localhost:5432. Connection details and demo credentials are fixed in the database method of ReservationApprovalPersistenceTests; changing Docker Compose variables alone does not change this test configuration.

git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
java -version
bash backend/mvnw -f backend/pom.xml --batch-mode --no-transfer-progress -Dtest=ReservationApprovalDesignTests,ReservationAuthorizationTests test
bash backend/mvnw -f backend/pom.xml --batch-mode --no-transfer-progress -Dtest=ReservationApprovalPersistenceTests test

headers: What remains before closing the assessment
rows: Record the teams, date and fixed baseline; retain run evidence.
Without these, B1/B2 and test results cannot be tied to a specific assessment.
Decide whether the proposed criterion and C05 evidence cover the required C04 scope.
Proposing a criterion does not prove completion or acceptance of the C04 deliverable.
Check the time context of the evidence and its references to ADR-01.
The conflicting Evidence C03B wording was corrected in this revision. Historical test counts remain historical results and cannot be reused as a current run.
For candidates, record the procedure, result and actual owner disposition.
An acknowledged risk or proposed action is not an executed test or an owner decision.

blocks.content: By the end of C06, it should be traceable what was assessed, on which version, using which procedure and with what result. Deliver the form with evidence for B1–B2, R1–R5, A1–A4, Q1–Q3 and D1–D5, records of examined candidates and the owner’s disposition. The purpose is to reach defensible conclusions and concrete next steps.
